The downside of this course comes with grades, there is very little room for you to mess up if you want a good grade, and there are quizzes almost every week. I did extremely well on most midterms but messed up on one and it tanked my grade. That being said, if you keep up with the coursework and do the practice she suggests, her exams are extremely fair. I truly felt like she made the course organized and doable. I would recommend taking her, just be careful with pacing your studying.

Great lecturer and really helped understand the material. Discussions are annoying to attend b/c of the discussion worksheets which are worth 8% of your grade. However, the worksheets are easy and if you get a good TA (shout out to Ziwen Gao) the quizzes are not too bad. Take Anna if you want to understand the material and do well in the class.

Alright professor, he wasn't particularly bad as a professor, but nor was he particularly good. He sometimes has trouble understanding the questions that he's being asked, and he usually responds in a very blunt and brief manner, which to some people may have come across as sassy or uncaring, but if you just keep asking your question and be patient, he'll try to answer the question. Anyways the major problem was that many things were not taught in the lecture and we had to learn them completely from scratch in the discussion or online when doing HW. Ultimately I don't think that's due to him being a bad teacher and more to do with the fact that Math141 is a weed out class and in general not built for student success.

Dr. S is one of the best Calc 2 professors to have. She doesn't waste any time deriving the formulas (which there are tons of) and gets straight to the point with examples (that appear on tests sometimes). Of course, you can ask her to derive them during her office hours, but I feel like her going over examples alone and explaining the concepts at the same time is more than enough. I felt very prepared for each of my midterms by just going to lecture, even with minimal studying. I will say the discussion worksheets become quite challenging, but the quizzes are extremely easy. I felt very prepared for the final this year and I recommend you sign up for Dr. S if you can. Calc 2 is not the horror story you hear if you take Dr. S and pay attention in lecture.

I really enjoyed having Pincus for 141. He is a very nice guy and you can tell he really cares about his students succeeding. He will answer any questions if you reach out and give full worked-out solutions to any homework/textbook problems you're struggling with. He also gives homework extensions if you need them and his exams are exactly like the homework and in-class examples he provides, they were all very fair and he is a pretty generous grader. His lectures were a bit dull but they worked, he writes on a piece of paper and projects it to the class and he basically just writes out the textbook definitions of the key concepts/theorems you need to know and then does examples. If you pay attention and enjoy math, the lectures will be enough to prepare you for exams; all I did to study for exams were the homework problems, and I was very well prepared for the final. For the harder topics like series, though, you definitely have to study outside of class and he gave a ton of practice problems on ELMS for those. Overall, Pincus was a great guy and if you take him he sets you up to succeed.

If you are expecting to actually learn from this class, then I suggest you do not take Amin. He goes through lectures very fast and often skips a bunch of steps to arrive at answers. There will be weekly quizzes but the possible quiz questions will be posted so all you really need to do is memorize them so you can get easy 100s on them. For the last midterm we had, he basically gave us the midterm problems in advance but just changed the numbers around. The homework assignments are all due the day before the final exam so I suggest you keep pace with them because THEY WILL PILE UP if you don't (speaking from experience). 
Overall, he is a nice guy and responds to homework questions fairly quickly but if you actually want to learn and understand calc 2, you will not get that from this prof. I'd say this class was more of an experience for me to learn how to study to pass rather than learn content (do what you will with this info).

i came into this class FOUR years after taking calc 1 (aka remembering nothing) and still managed to do decently okay. lectures were surprisingly useful and made me motivated to go and not get too far behind. her notes are clear and easy to follow and the quizzes were also useful to get some extra studying in before any exams came up. the final is horrendous but thats the final for all the math141 sections combined, so this is expected. your lowest exam becomes half credit and the lowest quiz gets dropped. there's a small curve beyond that but don't depend on it. i really recommend szczekutowicz!!

Paradela is a hit or a miss. If you have taken Calculus II or an equivalent course back in high school, you won't have many problems. If you are an older student like a sophomore who is starting their math education from scratch, you will unfortunately suffer. Although his exams are pretty easy and although he is somewhat honest about what we can expect to be on a quiz or midterm, his teaching methods aren't very useful. First of all, he reads straight out of the textbook and he also doesn't record the lectures because he uses a LITERAL chalkboard. Also, although it is understandable with 154 of us, he also takes FOREVER to grade exams. For example, I didn't get my first midterm back until the day after I had already taken the second midterm. I honestly think you may be better off reading the textbook and doing the practice problems compared to trying to pay attention during the lectures.

Not a great teacher, Jamie often writes very messy on the board which is sometimes compensated with all of his examples being from the textbook, but some units like complex numbers are not in there. Going to keystone tutoring was a necessity to complete some of the homework’s as even chatgbt and wolfram alpha would get them wrong and they’d be needlessly complicated for something that’s only 3% of the grade. Reading the textbook and going to TA office hours will help, but this is just a hard class in general especially if your last calculus class was AB in high school

I had to give this professor a low rating. His Spanish accent makes it difficult to understand him, pronouncing the word "derivative" as "daliwadi", affecting the learning experience. I think most of you Americans will be okay with the Spanish accent since I am an international student with English as a secondary language. If you say the accent part is my problem, then you just can't bear the rest. He uses examples only and directly from the textbook (the textbook, at the same time, doesn't cover the complex number part), offering no deeper explanations. His handwriting is also a mess, mixing around letters like "p" and "l" with confusing signs and symbols （like the sign "*"） that make it hard to follow in class. On top of all that, our midterm grades only come out right before the next midterm exam. The midterm exam's difficulties are still acceptable though (it gets harder every time), and the final exam is a little bit harder. But this doesn't help too much since the lectures are just a waste of time. 
However, I want to give a huge shoutout to the TA (this is why this comment is 2 stars instead of 1). The TA is incredibly interesting and understanding and always makes sure to explain things clearly. He also didn't give attendance credits to discussions right after midterms (I think he gets the point that nobody likes to rush to a discussion on Monday at 8 AM right after an exam). Grading is fair and easy, and he is super helpful when I’m seeking help after an absence from class, offering clear explanations and support ONLY for me for 20 MINUTES on a concept in his office. He deserves all the praise! 
But still, this has been a frustrating and unhelpful course due to the professor. This is my FIRST few months in the United States for my lifetime. I'd like to call this a terrible first experience. I ended up spending 90% of my time self-studying. I wouldn't recommend him to anyone.

I have to give this professor a low rating... First of all, his Spanish accent makes his course hard to understand, which affects the learning experience. For instance, he pronounces the word "derivative" as "deliwadi". If you say that the accent part is my problem, I will take it since I am an international student with English as a second language. But there's MORE. 
On top of that, he only uses examples directly from the textbook, offering no deeper explanations. His handwriting is a mess, with confusing signs and symbols that make it hard to follow in class. This includes messing up the letters "p" and "l", as well as strange signs like the "*". 
Finally, about the exams and assignments. The exams' difficulties are okay, just get harder every time. (my grades fell from 95 at the first midterm to 85 at the final) His grading is so slow that we can only get our midterm grades back after we take the NEXT midterm. The deadlines of assignments are strange sometimes (where we have to do homework assignments with materials not involved in class yet). The homework system is also hateful when it pops out "This question will award no credit after attempt 1" while other questions allow attempts up to 5 times. 
However, I want to give a huge shoutout to the TA. The TA is incredibly interesting and always makes sure to explain things clearly. He gave no attendance credits to the discussion right after a midterm exam. (I think he got the point that nobody wants to rush to a discussion at 8 AM right after a stressful exam) Grading is fair and easy, and they are super helpful when I’m absent, offering clear explanations and support ONLY FOR ME FOR 20 MINUTES in his office.
Sadly the excellent TA cannot save this course. This is my first few months in the United States of my lifetime. I ended up self-studying for 90% of the time. I'd like to call this course a bad first experience because it is just so disappointing. I will give 2 stars, all of them to the TA.

I had her for Calc 2 and I would say she's the best option among other professors. Her lectures are really helpful and easy to understand comparing to other professors. She also posts lecture notes and few practice problems (only for the hardest chapter tho). Quizzes are super easy (maybe it's just my TA). However, homework and discussion worksheets are graded so that requires you to go to discussion. But in the end we got to drop 5 hw and 5 worksheets so its not a big deal. Exams are lowkey a little challenging tho but if you spend time going over the sample exams and understand the chapter formulas, you should be fine. I would recommend her.

His lectures aren't great; sometimes he just rushes and quickly talks through fundamental concepts. However, he is a really nice guy & very understanding. His curve is also great!! This class was really hard for me, but study the material and read the textbook and you should be able to pass.

He posts all his notes ahead of class so a month into school I stopped going to all his lectures because they were pointless. I couldn't understand anything he was explaining and when people asked him questions, his response confused me more. However, the curve he implements at the end of the semester is really good. The material is hard, but it is possible to learn yourself by doing a crap ton of practice problems, looking at YouTube videos, and asking your peers. Basically, its a self study class. I know calc 2 is a weed out class, and this class is reflective of that, but its not impossible to get an A in here if you put in the time and work.

I was scared of this class before coming in because I had heard it was a weedout but if you take this professor I honestly don't think it's bad at all. Her lectures are in depth and easy to understand, the questions on her exams are almost always very fair and she gives you a lot of material to practice from beforehand. Additionally, I like how organized this professor is. She puts all her notes on canvas and the tests are always graded within a reasonable time. My only recommendation is that you sit near the front of the class otherwise she probably won't answer your question.

As an incoming freshman who has never taken Calc II before, I liked Jaime as a professor because he was straightforward with teaching and used a LOT of examples. He is very understanding of students because he always asks a lot of everything makes sense. He is also accommodating to students who may not be the brightest or have special needs. He may mess a few things up like homework dates or test questions, but fairly compensates and rectifies those mistakes by changing the dates or giving free points.

Paradela is not a teacher, he acts like a research professor who does not care to actually give lectures. He shows up late sometimes to the lectures, he writes messy on the chalkboard, can barely hear him in the back of the room, and administratively is a mess. I went from an A the entire year to a C+ after a slightly substandard final and a bunch of grades slammed in mid-December. My TA was relatively unhelpful too. He doesn't curve, except he does drop one exam which is nice. I stopped going to lecture to just teach myself the content.

Chill guy fr. Always posted notes from textbook and pretty much just went through the problems on those notes during lecture. You can earn bonus points in lecture for answering one of his questions or correcting a mistake he makes. Gives you 4 midterms so he can drop the lowest of the 4, and the last midterm is composed of questions from a question bank you are given ahead of time. Discussion quiz questions are also from a known set of textbook problems. Put effort into your quizzes and webassigns because according to the syllabus: "The lowest of {the second lowest test score, the average of 8 remaining quiz grades out of 100, the average of 28 remaining WA grades out of 100} will be replaced by the middle score among the three". This helped me go from a B+ to an A.

Amazing TA! Made worksheets for discussions and on quiz days those worksheets often had problems mirroring the ones on the quiz. He also gave us practice tests that I found very helpful for preparing for midterms.

Paradela is an okay professor. For the most part, his lectures were understandable unless it was the series and sequences unit, where I had no idea what was going on. His handwriting can sometimes be messy and difficult to understand. He will very often make mistakes when working out the problems. He would also have the HWs assigned incorrectly which was frustrating. I also thought him giving a quiz a week before the final was wrong. That being said, he is a chill dude and sometimes the class was lowkey comical. I thought his exams were very fair too. I would take him again if I had to, but would recommend trying someone else.

I stopped going to lectures after the month because I found I learned better from the textbook directly. 

10 quizzes - Each has two possible problems for the weekly chapter topics. Study them, practice them, everything, it will be worth it. The lowest two get dropped. 
30 webassigns - Do them, they're great practice, and easy 12.5% of your grade. The lowest two get dropped. You won't really need the drops but it's a good just in case.
4 midterms on each unit - Study for them well, textbook suggested problems are good practice, ask your TAs or go talk to Amin. If you need to, watch Prof Leonard on youtube. He drops the lowest exam.

After drops, he replaces the lowest grade

I think overall this teacher was just okay. To clarify first, this class with this teacher only really gets more difficult as the semester goes on. As a person, the teacher was just okay, he was very chill but also didn't really care that much in general (good and bad thing i guess?). Answering questions he wouldn't really clearly answer it and it was clear that most people in the class wouldn't understand what he was talking about. For teaching, I felt that he was an alright teacher at the start but as the class got more rigorous it got increasingly more difficult to understand what he was teaching. For HW, I would give it maybe 1.5/5 stars due to just how ridiculously hard they could be and sometimes just unrelated the material was to what was being taught. For TA, I had Cameron Yeagle and I would give him 5 stars just how helpful and friendly he was, much much better teacher than the professor I felt. If you can, try to find a different professor.

Stopped attending lectures after the 2nd week cause they were pretty pointless. Doing the textbook problems will prepare you well. Amin seems like a nice guy but doesn't teach well lecture style. I'm sure if you meet with him one-on-one he can teach better. TA's weren't much help either. If you are not good at self-studying then you should probably take someone else.

Anna is an amazing professor. She understands how difficult calculus 2 is to comprehend and makes sure to teach you all of the difficult problems as well as give you challenging problems on the worksheets. Anna explained and broke down every topic to it's roots. It is clear how much she enjoys teaching the class along with her in-depth understanding of the subject. 

-Exams were difficult but never threw tricks at you
-Lots of homework
-TA's were super helpful

The professor was clearly knowledgeable about the topics covered and did do a lot of review before exams in class. While the discussions could have been better, I think the lectures were useful. There was a lot of information to cover over the semester, meaning she wasn't always able to clarify material, but that was primarily due to time constraints as well as the class size. The discussions and quizzes were not very helpful, but I think that mainly was due to the TA not being very good at explaining the concepts.
The main issue was with the homework. I didn't like the way the Cengage (for HW) worked. It was really picky about formats like case sensitivity. It also would sometimes not understand work given and would refuse to grade it. Since it was never graded manually, it would sometimes mark correct work wrong because it had a slightly different format. This also meant that feedback on homework was either vague or nonexistent, which would be my biggest criticism of the course. While it was only worth 3% of the grade, it certainly would have benefited me to have more immediate feedback beyond correct or incorrect.

Fantastic professor and explains concepts very well. Only negative interaction I ever had was when asking if she was going to post sample final exam solutions to study. She found this very rude and made me very aware of that fact, saying she wouldn't and to solve them myself (I had not asked her to solve them for me). Sample exams and solutions are available, as I got them from other friends, so just ask around from friends in other courses if you can't find them in the test bank. Just try to be respectful when talking to her and the class will be great.

This was one of the easiest "weed out" classes and Jaime was a big part on why it was so easy. The content itself is just formulas, as he said at the beginning of the course that there would be no proofs, so as long as you know the formulas, you'll be fine for the course. He tells you the formulas, sometimes can be a little confusing but if you look at the textbook to double check, you'll be good. I agree with the previous reviews that some of the letters and signs he uses are pointless and confusing, but I'll give him a pass b/c it's his second sem of teaching. 
His midterms are very easy, often using 1-2 questions that were done in class. Averages were objectively good (82, 90, 80, 69) with the worst midterm average being the student's problem (A series test w/o Taylor series). The structure questions on the midterms are similar to the ones on the final. The grading does take a little while but it's not a big deal. The HW is a hassle but it's only 3% of the grade so you just gotta do the best you can.
As for him answering questions, I didn't have an issue with the ways he answered them, especially with the number of bad questions that were asked (questions like someone asking why put an "x" next to pi when integrating pi in dx terms). To the students who are going to take this course or anything like it: don't blindly ask questions. Actually try to understand it first.
I recommend taking Jaime to the people that like a little more independence or already have taken BC calc. If you want a more traditional approach where the prof does all the work, look elsewhere.

Jaime is a great teacher. While his lecture style is a little dull, he explains the content thoroughly and his office hours are very helpful. They were often pretty sparsely attended, so when I went to his office hours, I basically had one-on-one tutoring. He was very open to students asking questions and I felt like I could much better understand the content with his explanations outside of class. If you don't want to put in that effort, then maybe he's not the best teacher for you, but I really enjoyed learning with him over the course of the semester.

Dr. Szczekutowicz is a model instructor. She gave me everything I needed to learn Calculus 2. Excellent lectures that concisely and clearly explained every unit, and always had examples that introduced the more difficult problem types. She always gave us problems that prepared us for the upcoming exam, a trait that I feel is critical for a class like MATH141. Her exams her very fair, and I felt like she wanted me to succeed the entire time. When I went into office hours to get help, she didn't just answer my question, but helped me 'think' about how to best use the toolbox of integral solving methods. I got a 88% on the final, and I could not have done it without Dr. Szczekutowicz as my teacher. If Dr. Szczekutowicz is listed as an instructor for any future course I take, I would pick again her in a heartbeat.
garbage. hard to hear, not good at explaining topics. messy notes. calc 2 is one of the hardest classes here and he doesn't help.

This teacher does absolutely nothing. He doesn’t get up from his desk and just reads slides online to his students. Most people I know don’t go to any of his lectures because they are comically basic…he just sits there reading his slides.

TLDR: Show up to every class & discussion, do your assigned problems, and show up to office hours since he's 100% willing to help.
I've been wanting to write this review for a while, as someone who took Dr. Williams for 140, currently taking him for 141 and planning on taking him for 241. I'm going to say that he's a good professor and a fair grader.

One thing I did not do in 140 that I do now that helps a ton is going to office hours. When I say that his office hours are life savers, I truly mean it. He's literally open to explaining material and guiding you through everything that it is CRIMINAL not to go. And even if you don't have him, as long as he's teaching your course that semester you can still show up and get help. I cannot stress this enough, his office hours are literally just three hours a week of him just helping people with various stuff (textbook problems, WebAssigns, etc). 

Another thing that Williams does is take problems verbatim from the textbook. 9/10 you can find the textbook online, but even if its a paper version, BRING IT TO CLASS. Williams will literally assign problems directly from the textbook onto our exams. I can confidently say that if you do 10% of the textbook problems from each section, you'll be guaranteed an B on each exam. 

Make sure you also attend lecture as much as possible, as Williams LOVES to put problems we directly went over in lecture on our exams. On our most recent exam, the last problem was something he had done two classes ago. If you attend lecture and do his recommended problems, you should be passing pretty comfortably.

When it comes to discussion sections, from my experience I'd also try to go to them. They're a lot harder than what he puts on the exams, but still great practice.

My only critique for him has to be how we do not have any recorded lectures this semester (he was recording for 140) and that if you miss one class/take one bad set of notes, it could set you back severely depending on the content. Otherwise, he's a great professor!
Greatest TA you can ask for, he knows the answer to any math questions you ask, easily understandable as well.
Definitely take him if you have the chance! Lectures are very straightforward, always extends homeworks, and very fair exams. I also had TA Lixin and he is great.

Genuinely and unfortunately a terrible professor. He just reads from slides and gives "practice questions" for you to do and expects you to understand them with no context and little to no explanation. It's basically like if you gave someone a pencil that has no lead and expected you to write them an essay. He also tries to make painfully unfunny jokes that never land well and his lectures (before I stopped going) had an incredibly awkward vibe. The only good thing about this course is he offers lecture videos that are higher quality than his actual teaching. I remember he did like a Dracula accent on the first day of class and dropped it halfway through with no acknowledgement. His exams are made to trick you, and he is crazily unhelpful & straight up creepy with some of the comments he makes. I wouldnt wish this course on anyone. I only got stuck with him due to the late registration dates that freshmen get, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!

Language barrier, messy chalkboard writing, blocks his writing until he moves onto the next thing, no lecture recordings. Despite all this, I still enjoyed his class, though my discussion TA carried hard for certain topics. The professor himself is a pretty funny guy once you get to know him, and he does want you to pass, despite what you might think. He has multiple ways to explain concepts if you don't understand. This is a class where I'd recommend sitting at the front, but it's manageable.

From someone who struggled in calculus 1, Dr.Gruber did everything in his power to ensure my class is on track to pass. I'm talking revisiting topics for extra points, extending deadlines on homework, an entire website dedicated to the notes we take in his class??? One of the only math professors that show an ounce of empathy to his students. You deserve someone who's flexible and is willing to help you succeed, Sean Gruber is that someone! But also keep in mind he's putting a lot of work to ensure you succeed, so just make sure you're not waiting his time and actually use the several resource he is providing.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. If you are taking math141 or any math class take it with professor gruber. I took calc 1 with a different professor and found calc 2 was easier, which is mostly due to the professor I had. He actually cares about his students and posts all lecture videos online and also has a lot of notes and resources. Quizzes every Thursday that took 10 minutes and were very easy if you kept up with the class. I didn't go to lecture very much but when I went they were engaging and he relied a lot on student feedback. 

Exams 1 and 2 were very doable and people often only used half the time given. If you do the homework then it is almost exactly what is on the exam. Exam 3 was more difficult but also very similar to the homework. The averages were high on exams 1 and 2 but he still gave some points back for exam 1. For exam exam 3 the average was low so he awarded a lot of points back as well. He weighs your lowest exam score to 10% instead of 20%. The homework was only about 4 or 5 questions a week and did not take that much time to do as well. 

Overall calc 2 can be challenging but Sean Gruber gives you so many opportunities to succeed, so actually take this class with him it will literally save your grade.

My GOAT!!! Absolutely best TA a person could ask for. Covered so much material every discussion, cleared up any confusions we had as a class. He was a lifesaver for the weekly quizzes as he briefly explained what the questions would be formatted like prior to the quiz. An even bigger lifesaver for the exams as the day before each exam he would give us fantastic review problems. Without Dmitrii idk how I would have gotten through this MATH141. Dmitrii if you're reading this I love you.

The absolute best math prof I've ever had in my life!!! He cares so much about every student, it's almost surreal. Everything he does is for our benefit, and he always wants our input on how he can improve his lectures and exams. 
His lectures are super informative and actually interesting, his exams are extremely fair, and he just made me feel so reassured coming into MATH141, as I was super worried about it. 

DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN TO TAKE HIS CLASS!
I LOVE DR GRUBER!!!!
Great prof and very helpful. Easy exams and minimal required homework. He posts lecture recordings.

Really great professor. Goes slower than most when covering topics in lecture, and sometimes unnecessary, but cant complain about that. Quizzes and exams are identical to worksheet problems and homework, so do those and you're good. Gives a curve if averages are below 70 on exams. Really accommodating in terms of redoing assessments and just generally a really great professor. if you can I highly recommend taking him even if its an 8 am its worth it.

Good Professor does difficult examples in lecture, and uploads the lecture notes which is insanely helpful. The exams are challenging, but he gives review problems to drive your thoughts on the topics, they are not the same questions with different numbers which I thought was pretty good.

Dr. Gruber IS THE BOYYYYYYYYY. The best math professor I'VE EVER HAD. He records and posts all lectures, his discussion worksheets and homework are both super short and due only once a week, and he is just an overall amazing lecturer. I'd recommend him to anybody.

Chadwick is actually fantastic. He goes over examples very slow in class which is very helpful to understanding the subjects. His exams I always found to be super fair, never overcomplicating questions, just testing your basic knowledge. In the off chance he put an unpredictable question on the exam, he would drop hints at it during lecture. My TA, Ben, was great, very knowledgeable and patient when explaining questions. He also drops a lot of things and is very nice with his grade cutoffs. Overall, highly recommend taking him if you have the chance.

Chadwick is a great teacher and his lectures feel well planned and organized. He is generally very accommodating around making up exams and he will extend homework pretty often if he doesn't cover everything in class. Overall great guy and fair professor.

Very good teacher, super nice, and explains concepts well. The best part of her class is that she gives you neat lecture notes in the course files. Her exams are a little hard and long, but I believe she adequately prepares you. If you read the reviews of last semester, it says the discussions are really long and hard. She told my class that she made them more easier and I think they are okay. Even though you can't pick your TA, Harrison is very good.

Best professor for calc 2 for sure, her lectures are really well structured and digestible. I had to do webassigns for calc 1 as homework and most of the time was just looking up answers to get credit, but the homework/quiz format she used this semester helped me a lot. Basically she posts weekly homeworks that you don't turn in, and on most Tuesdays during discussion you have a quiz that's very similar to one of the problems on the homework. As long as you understand and work through those it's easy points. Discussion worksheets were pretty tedious but the content was always covered beforehand in lecture. Exams were a bit tough but fair, every single question was similar to or exactly a question on the homework or discussion worksheets. I found the final a lot easier than any of the midterms so understanding the homeworks and worksheets + the structure of past exams will prepare you very well. Calc 2 is generally a hard class so as long as you put in the time for this class you'll have everything you need to do well with Dr. S.

Best TA I've ever had! Unfortunately, I thought my calc 2 professor was very difficult to work but Cameron was so kind and super friendly and helpful. I honestly thought he taught better than my calc professor and he would be kind enough to teach us the concepts that would be on the quiz right before the quiz so we'd understand how to approach them. He is very patient and understanding, and I think (again) teaches in a very clear, concise way. I wish I could have him again as a TA! He literally brought pastries to his 8 AM second to last discussion for us to eat. I literally have no complaints at all!

OMG this professor has to be the best professor at UMD. I PASSED CALC 1 WITH A C AND PASSING THIS CLASS, CALC 2, WITH AN A. his exams are SUPER EASY.  he never gave any jumpscare problems on any exams. ALSO the TAs were amazing. I guarantee that if you go to every discussion, you won't even need to do the homeworks. Quizzes are very easy as well and both the professor and the TA prepares you well for them. A little side note: homework is worth like 2% of your grade so you're better off focusing on the quizzes, worksheets in discussions, and exams as they are worth a lot. If you have to wait on the waitlist, do it.

Dr. Chadwick is probably my favorite professor this semester! He was very helpful, and I found his lectures to also be very helpful. He is an understanding professor so I would say communicate. Great professor and you can't go wrong with him. Highly recommend Dr. Chadwick!

Overall Anna was an amazing professor! Her explanations were usually clear and when they were not her published notes were easy to understand. The weekly homework and quiz were never super difficult just graded very harshly (but I believe this is more of a TA thing). The homework really did help to reinforce what was taught in class and never felt like busy work or anything. Her tests and grading were significantly more difficult compared to some other professors this semester. The exam reviews posted before exams were very good providing 50+ problems to work though.

Absolutely phenomenal professor. Her lectures were so easy to digest, she did detailed notes and step by step examples. She understands how difficult calc 2 is and she makes sure to take time on the difficult topics. She posted every lecture note and sometimes extra examples we did not have time for in lecture. Even though she posts all the notes, she often says important information in lecture that is not written down. There was no required homework but there was a weekly problem set posted and we had weekly one question quizzes in discussion that featured a very similar question from the hw. These problem sets were lengthy and often difficult, though the day of the quiz the TA went over the problems we had questions on and explained them before we took the quiz. The discussion worksheets could be difficult but they were helpful. I felt extremely prepared for the exams as the questions on it were similar to the homework, quizzes, or in class examples. She also gave two practice exams before exams so you got a sense of what you will see. For reference, I am not extremely gifted in math and got a C+ in calc 1 (different professor) and an A in calc 2. This learning style was extremely helpful to me. She gives all the tools you need to succeed. If she is available take Dr S!!!!

Great professor. Exams are very similar to practice questions and pretty easy, regardless. Homework is graded based on completion, and essentially, it is your curve. The final exam is not written by him, so it is definitely harder and different style of questions, but nothing you can do about that. Lectures are recorded, and he is an a overall great guy and good professor.
This professor is probably the worst person and professor I have ever encountered at this university. He doesn’t how to teach and is very disrespectful.

I've had Dr. Chad for both MATH141 and 140. After taking him for one full year, I can confidently say that he is a great teacher and might even be the best calc teacher at UMD. For MATH141, to achieve an A, you have to get above a 90 instead of 93. Additionally, he basically gives you 20 points of extra credit because he drops 20 points from the web assigns at the end of the semester. He also lowers the lowest mid term grade to be out of 50. For example, if you got an 80/100 he will turn it into a 40/50. He also drops a quiz and 3 worksheets. He posts all his notes in canvas. His notes are so good that even though I don't pay attention in his class at all, I still understand the notes perfectly. I've literally only studied the day before all the midterm tests and still averaged 95's because his notes are very clear. Additionally, the best part about taking his class is that the practice tests that he gives are almost exactly like the actual test. Overall, I really recommend taking Dr. Chadwick for both 141 and 140 because of how easy it is to get an A and also because of how easy he makes it to understand the concepts. (I did already take calc in high school).

Dr. Gruber is a kind-hearted, understanding, and passionate professor. He is always willing to answer questions and give summaries of each topic. Also, he is willing to go step by step through each problem to make sure everyone understands. He records all his lectures and creates extra videos to clarify problems from class. Moreover, he always makes it clear what he expects of us on exams, quizzes, and homework, and updates us via email. The lectures are extremely interactive and collaborative. While exams are 80% of the total grade, they resemble homework and quiz questions and are appropriately structured. Occasionally, there are curves/extra credit as well. The weekly quizzes greatly resemble the homework, and the homework and discussion problems are manageable and extremely helpful in better understanding the content. In many instances, Dr. Gruber and the TA go over the homework problems. I’d recommend doing as much practice for each topic, and you should have the opportunity to be successful.

Class was not too bad. Final was kinda hard so watch out for that. I never went to class so I cannot speak for Anna, but the notes she uploaded to Canvas were pretty helpful and taught me almost everything. Quizzes and Midterms were pretty solid.

"Oh Dr. Gruber, where do I begin?" :')

This man is the epitome of an amazing professor. He CARES, like he genuinely cares about his students and wants to make sure everyone does well and understands the material. He is so organized and communicates often to make sure everyone gets the memo and is up to date. He records his lectures and even records himself on his phone in case he writes on the board instead of his iPad. This is a man who goes above and beyond to make sure his students get the learning they pay for. I will say the only downside about him is that he tends to go slower than other professors, but who is complaining? I was glad at times that he did because he made CALC2 (an already difficult class) less difficult than it should be. I genuinely understand CALC2 so well now that I feel confident in future math classes. I wish that I had him for every math class here on out, but one can only be so lucky. Anyways, please do yourself the favor of picking this man as your professor, you will NOT regret it, ever.

Everyone speaks very highly of her and that's why I chose her as my teacher. But, I disagree with most of the comments. She goes too quickly in lectures and its hard to listen to her and take notes at the same time so I would focus on writing down what she was doing and I missed everything she was saying. There was a quiz every tuesday in discussion which is super annoying but you review right before. So depending on your TA, you can do really good or really bad. I think the midterms were way harder than other teachers and the final was just a lost cause. She posts her notes though so I appreciate that. I guess if you try really hard to stay on track and do practice problems everyday then you can do it but this class was so hard and I don't want to take her again.

Great professor all around. 

I came into calc 2 having failed AP Calc and only 1 college level calculus course under my belt which didn't even cover integration and managed to do better than I expected. Every lecture was well organized and she makes every topic easy to understand. She would introduce a new topic and then spend a majority of the time doing practice problems. She posts her notes so missing a class is not detrimental. 

Homework was not mandatory this semester which is apparently a new thing she's trying out. However I highly recommend you still do them as they are great practice. Most weeks there is a worksheet and quiz you do in discussion. The quizzes are just one problem to solve and are sometimes the same as a homework problem, and the TA's go over homework's before the quizzes anyways. The exams were fair and apparently she cut down from 4 midterms to 3 this semester, all of which had similar problems to homeworks and worksheets so doing the homework, even though its not graded, is great practice.

Having Foivos as your TA will be the best decision you make if taking MATH141! Calc 2 is difficult, but he makes it manageable and breaks down difficult concepts so that you actually understand what you’re learning. Math is not my strong suit, and this was the first math class that actually made sense, and it was due to his teaching style. He genuinely cares about his students and always makes time to help students when they are stuck or struggling. Even with the head injury I received while taking his course, he was able to accommodate and teach, which I feel says a lot about his character! Don’t second guess it—if you have a pulse, take Foivos!

Yea there's basically nothing bad to say. Every review has basically already covered it. He's incredibly nice and understanding. And you'll walk out of the class learning something while having a good time. If you have the option to take him, do it!
BEST PROFESSOR EVER. He taught me the entire course on 1 week. Complete clarity. Would highly recommend taking his class. He's going places.

I think I mainly disliked this class because the content is pretty difficult and if you're someone that doesn't like math or isn't great with it then you may have a hard time. Dr. Ebrahimian does do a pretty good job at lecturing and doesn't give any homework. He's a funny guy and his TAs are all really good. He isn't really the most chill grader and also gives no extra credit and no curve. Basically, he's a great teacher if you're looking to better understand content and less worried about your grade.

Great guy, great professor, great lectures. Posts good YouTube videos and tons of support. No bad questions in his class and he has a great sense of humor. Would 100% recommend taking this professor if you can.

One of the worst math professors you could take. Should have at least a 2 or lower. An insane percentage of the class drops his classes, leaving the kids who have to take it but struggled on the first exam completely screwed because there is NO curve. Exam averages are in the low to mid 60s. Almost anyone I have talked to has between a 65 and a 75 in his class. With no curve this should be illegal. Cannot imagine why anyone would want to take this guy.

I LOVE YU-CHI. Literally an angel of a TA. If you have to take Calc 2, I hope you get him as your TA. He always goes out of his way to answer questions and help with work, providing additional office hours if people need them and posting notes in his free time to better help explain material. If you don't understand a topic during the lecture, you will after the discussion with him.

I found her lectures easy to follow and loved the way she did example problems. She color-codes all of her example problems and posts them to review later, clearly titling each by topic. She also occasionally includes asides that are not graded, but fun to know and connect the material to other concepts. Her practice exams are very similar to the exams. The exams and quizzes often tested the more basic scenarios of the concepts taught in class, which was nice because there wasn't a lot of extra mathematical fluff to lose points on. There were graded worksheets almost every discussion and quizzes in discussion almost every week (except for exam weeks), so discussions are basically mandatory, but they also help a lot in understanding the material so I would recommend attended regardless of the graded assignments. "Homework" problems were available for extra practice if you wanted, but there was no graded homework, which is nice.
One of the worst math professors, refuses to curve anything and writes exams 1 day before giving them. Extension/Retake policy is needlessly strict and makes the class way harder than it has to be.

gave an exam on halloween :((( very nice and sweet, but is a little confusing when she lectures. she is too thorough when explaining easy concepts and then tends to rush the more difficult ones. she is very transparent about what will be on the quiz or exam. literally just do the practice exam and maybe some extra review and you'll be good. also you can skip her lectures, attendance is not mandatory at all and she posts the notes. if you do go to lecture she also doesn't cold call on people, which is nice. overall not the worst because she is really a well-meaning professor.

Dr. Ebrahimian is a very passionate and caring professor, and you can really tell that he loves what he does. He has a good sense of humor and is really helpful, so I would 100% recommend taking him. The class consists of weekly quizzes and hw submissions, 3 tests, and a final (30% of your grade). The class itself it honestly hard and fast paced, but I don't blame that on the professor, its more of the nature of Math141.

Really good teacher, all notes are well organized and are uploaded online after every class. Tests are easier than other professors, worksheets are lenient as the TA only grades a few questions rather than the entire worksheet. Also for quizzes, Dr. Song basically tells us the exact question type that will be on the quiz so there is very minimal studying that is needed to be done.
I have no words. It brings tears to my eyes that people like him still exist. He revived my passion for Math. He truly wants you to do well. TAKE HIM

You can't really ask for much more out of a Calc 2 professor. He posts notes after every lecture and has weekly surveys so you can let him know what was going well and what wasn't. I could really tell that he cared about teaching and wanted the best for us. He is a very generous grader and probably makes Calc 2 the most "enjoyable" it can be at this school.
Super great professor. His lectures are helpful, and he posts videos on youtube too. Exams are fair, gives you practice exams that are very similar, and wants everyone to succeed.

Professor song is a very nice person but not a good professor, at all. Having taken calc 2 before with other professors, I can confidently say her explanations of the topics are incredibly confusing and she does a horrible job of preparing her students for the exams. When trying to simplify complex ideas and arithmetic, she actually makes them even harder to understand and does not go over important topics/formulas which are on the final and midterms. You  are better off taking another professor and self studying for the class using videos/online notes.

the way he taught concepts was okay and was very receptive to questions and helpful during office hours, however the way he wrote problems for exams and homeworks were almost criminal. i had to withdraw from the class after the 2nd exam to save my gpa even after countless hours of studying, going to office hours, asking questions, doing practice problems, etc. just the way the problems in exams are written are horrible and there's no curve.

Literally a great instructor, his tests are very hard but he gives you all the material you need. Is ALWAYS more than happy to answer questions and help students, you can tell he’s very passionate about his job and teaching. Great upstanding guy and good lecturer, despite the demanding class.

Jonathan is an extremely knowledgeable professor! He provides a lot of practice problems for the quizzes and exams, which makes it so much easier to know what to expect on the actual exams. His exams are very similar to the practice exams that he and his TAs go over in class and discussion, so if you put in the work, you'll be well prepared.

His TA's this semester were amazing as well. They were super helpful and always gave a bunch of tips and tricks on how to solve some difficult questions. They held a bunch of office hours throughout the semester and closer to the final. The TAs every discussion went over the worksheets thoroughly and the notes were posted after the worksheets were due.

Jonathan himself is a very chill guy. He had office hours throughout the week and you can always pop in to ask questions about the class and even just to chat about random things. He curved the midterms a LOT, which helped everyone's grades. He genuinely cares for his students performance and our mental health, especially around exam time. He also shares a lot of words of wisdom and funny remarks in lecture, which makes the class entertaining sometimes.

The only downside is that he sometimes goes on small tangents or starts deriving random formulas, but overall I'd say that the lectures were pretty organized and easy to follow. He also had a zoom each class, so you could always join if you were not able to make it to a lecture. The zooms were recorded each time as well so you can always look back on them as a resource later in the semester. And he always posted his notes from lecture on canvas.

GOAT TA for MATH141. She was always really kind to her students and offered a bunch of tips when solving difficult problems. At the beginning of the semester, she would talk really quickly and do the problems really fast, but after a couple of students asked for her to slow down a bit, it was perfectly fine. She offers a bunch of office hours and is available at other times as well if you ever have to make up a quiz or exam.

Before the quizzes, she would always give our class sample questions that were really similar to the quiz. And before exams, she went over sample exams and always published her detailed notes in the ELMS class. 10/10 TA, would recommend.

(Note: this review comes from someone who has taken Calc 2/MATH141 equivalent at another institution prior, so review may be bias slightly.)

Overall, a very good professor. He records his lectures via Zoom and also has shared notes via ScribbleTogether, which is very helpful if ever sick or unable to attend lecture in person. However, do not just use these alone; go to his lecture. Dr. Fernandes has a good energy and good method of running his class and in a way feels relatable. He is very humble and relatable, as while small errors come in, he can easily fix and wants to work with the class. He connected ideas in real life and other fields to Calc 2, which I found the connections interesting. He presented the analogy of our knowledge being described as graphs, and their derivatives being positive, and that stuck throughout the semester. He wants to teach you and he works well. He goes through the content in depth and gave me some “wow” moments when an idea that did not previously connect from the other Calc 2 course I took finally connected. Overall, honored to learn from someone like him.

Literally the GOAT. Lectures and exams were straight forward, he recorded lectures, posted his notes, and is overall a just an amazingly friendly guy. He provided practice exams for the midterm and final, which were very helpful. Overall, he just made his tests very fair and prepared us well for the final. Absolutely would recommend Dr. Fernandes for 141 in the future.

Dr. Ebrahimian is the best to ever do it.   A great professor with a fantastic sense of humor.  He does a really good job at answering any question and breaks down the concepts in a comprehensible manner.  There are 3 exams and a final, and he posts past exams, which are very similar to the actual thing.  The weekly quizzes make sure that you are on top of your content, and the worksheets every other discussion boost your grade.  The TAs were also great and extremely helpful.  Overall, I hope I have a professor as good as him in the future, and definitely take him if you can.

Ebrahimian is a great professor. He's insanely smart but explains everything really well. As someone who struggles with calculus, I appreciated his teaching style. Lectures are basically just example problems, but people are pretty engaged and he'll answer any questions that pop up. Weekly quizzes in discussion which are a little annoying but they do force you to study the topics one at a time so you don't cram it all before the exam. Exams are pretty standard, not insanely hard or easy. He also posts lecture videos on YouTube which are great if you have to miss a lecture or just don't feel like going.
The goat. If you ever have an opportunity to take him as a prof take him. I once had an issue with grading and he fixed it immediately. He is phenomenal at lecturing, and he is very funny. Take him!!

Dr Williams was honestly a great professor. He is always open to answering questions and his test are very fair if you do his suggested problems and hw, sometimes they are even the same questions. The final was decently harder than the rest of his test but thats to be expected. If you have the opportunity to take Dr. Williams definitely do so. He also doesn’t do minuses which is nice for GPA.

I just finished taking Calc 2 with Fernandes, and I have to say, in the beginning, the class was a bit rough. As a lecturer, he can go into tangents and sometimes teach a more difficult way to solve a problem. I think I would have had a much more difficult time if I didn't take Calc BC in high school. The discussions by his TA's are really helpful and make sure you go through every worksheet before an exam. If you can do the worksheets without any help then you are fine for the exams, but they are pretty hard. I also think this did help, though, because eventually he does curve the exams and the final by a few points which really does help, and the final was a lot easier then any exam he had given in class. If you asked me at the start of the year, I would have given him a 2 star because it is a rough start, but overtime things start coming together and you eventually get used to it.

imma tell you right now this is one of the best professors you can expect to get for any math class. covered all bases was clear on expectations answers questions sharply and the pace of the class is very tight. if you fail it really is just a skill issue.

TAKE HIS CLASS ANY CHANCE YOU GET!

He recently started teaching an actual class instead of being a TA, and he does an amazing job. His teaching style is very easy to follow; he introduces the concept and immediately follows with examples that would resemble sort of questions that would appear on exams. He really prepares you well for the finals. 
Some fun fact: he uses chalk on black boards and walkthroughs concepts, its derivations, and examples along with students which makes it so much engaging! [I note this because some professors would have a problem already solved and would go piece by piece on a presentation which I find not much engaging and helpful]

Overall, he knows his stuff and definitely cares about his students. If he ever teaches a higher level course, I will take it immediately.

She is a very considerate professor and wants you to succeed. Her worksheets and quizzes were very reasonable and not difficult at all. Prior to quizzes she even tells you what type of problems will be on the quiz during lecture. Song responds to emails very quickly and Jen was also a wonderful TA. Some worksheets are also dropped at the end of the semester along with your lowest quiz score. Math is not my strong suit which is why I barely passed, but if you complete every quiz and worksheet, that should create a nice cushion in case you don't do well on the exams. Speaking of exams, she also gives very helpful study guides.
Good lecturer, very supportive professor, recommend him for anyone. He gets the important information across very well, and is available for any help that anyone needs. Generally an awesome guy.

Did not enjoy this professor throughout the semester. His lectures are engaging sometimes. Most of the time he goes off tangents, like really hard problems that we would never see on exams. There are weekly quizzes in discussion, but they are basically useless because the TAs write them and not him. And the TAs have no idea what is going on. The best resource is the textbook problems, one time he literally pulled one of those and put it on the exam. But his exams are extremely difficult, as are many calc 2 exams. I don't recommend him. Anyone else!!

The goat. Posts videos online, has practice exams released to use to study that are actually super similar to the actual exams. Drops the 2 lowest quizzes, 2 lowest worksheets, and replaces your lowest exam grade with your final exam grade only IF you do better on the final exam. All his TA's are nice. Overall funny guy, good professor, and actually tries his best to help you end with a good grade.

Professor Ebrahimian is a great professor. His examples in class relate to the worksheet although it can be challenging which is expected for math141. He makes jokes here and there. His explanations are good as well. He does post youtube videos of his lectures. I would one thousand percent recommend going to discussion and hopefully if your TA is good you’ll feel better about this class. He also gives a fair amount of time to review for exams. A downside of him is that his lectures are really fast and some of the assigned homework problems are unnecessary. Overall, I think he is a great professor for math141 and would recommend taking his class.

Honestly a goat of a prof, if i focused any more in this class and had a little better time management this sem i could've easily secured an A. Had a great TA as well which also helped as i just mainly learnt the content through my discussions. Didn't go to lectures much as it was a little confusing but everything else about the class was perfect.

An Amazing Lecturer, provides great resources, has his own Youtube channel with content for each of his classes and then some. Also, he answers questions very well and expects the students to follow content with him. He will ask the class to help him solve something. Super Awesome. If you go to lecture, pay attention, and study a little, you will do fine with Ebrahimian. 

He drops the lowest couple of assignments, and will use your final to replace a midterm exam grade (if it is higher). So there is some semblance of a curve.

My advice, study extensively, and do very well on the midterms. Then you won't have to try so hard on the final.

One of the few professors I looked forward to seeing. Felt like I was learning. GOAT

Honestly speaking I can tell the Jonathan cares about how well his students do in his class. He is not one of those professors who go out their way to make the class hell. He wants you to do well. However, his teaching style can be bad to most. He doesn't go over that many example problems and even most of the problems in his notes are left unfinished. You will have to rely a lot on outside studying. You can't get through the class with just going to the lectures. I found out his lectures weren't doing much for me so I actually stopped going and only went to discussions. He also records his lectures so you don't have to be worried about missing lectures. Who you have as your TA also helps a lot. My TA went over HW problems/solutions and for our quizzes she would go over very identical problems right before. Which made it easier to do good on the quizzes. I completely bombed the 3 midterms we had. The first 2 I went in very unprepared so thats understandable but the third one I actually studied and I did terrible. Keep in mind that last unit is very challenging so try your best on the first midterms. Honestly, I was scared I wouldn't pass the class but I locked in for the final and got a decent score. Jonathan also had very generous curves. He curved all our midterms so they were out of either 90 or 95 out of the total 105 total points available. He also curved the HW/quizzes. And he also replaced our lowest midterm grade with our final grade if we did better on the final. That helped me a lot. Overall, I would suggest taking him. The curves may not be that helpful to people that are in the higher percentile but I think thats how all curves are designed.
Honestly an amazing teacher, calc 2 is so hard but you can tell he actually wants every student to succeed, and will put in the time and effort to make sure you do!

I had Foivos as my professor and he was amazing. Lectures were very fast paced and it was hard to understand at times, but he was amazing with helping you understand outside of class. He held office hours twice a week at the beginning of the course and would often go overtime just to help. Closer to finals season he added more and at one point there was four a week. He truly cares about his students and he gives you all the materials you need to succeed!

Jonathan is a great professor. He records lectures and has zoom meetings if you just want to do the lecture from your bed. The discussions are really helpful and the TAs are amazing. One quiz a week and one worksheet per discussion, which we go over in discussion, so it should mostly be a free 100. quizzes are easy as TAs go over practice problems that are basically the same questions as the quiz right before. Exams are 6 questions each with some having part A and B. Exams are out of 105 with a 5 point buffer. They are pretty fair as long as you review, just make sure that you do, otherwise there will be a couple questions you get wrong and with only 6 questions, it counts for a lot of the grade. Curve is insane as the exams will be put out of 95 or 90 depending on the average and the final will replace your worst exam grade if it's better. worksheets and quizzes are also curved so the worst one is dropped. Unfortunately the final is not curved, but that's made up for with all the other curves. Overall really simple class, I didn't even go to lecture after the first couple weeks and just watched the parts I needed. Discussion is more important and more useful for worksheets and quizzes. Honestly, I learned more from discussion than from lecture. Make sure to make a study group with those in your lecture, they will be really helpful to study with.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Pincus. I took him through Freshman Connection. His quizzes are based on the homework, exams are fair (similar to practice ones he gives), and he genuinely cares about his students. He can tell if you're putting in an effort. I thought I bombed the final, and it was his generosity that made me end with the grade I wanted (with the final in I would've ended with a lower grade for sure). Apart from the fact that some of his lectures are confusing and you have to self-learn concepts, he is an AMAZING professor, and I highly recommend him. Since Calc 2 is a hard class in general, you have to put in effort and definitely hours of studying, but if you do that, you're chilling in his class.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Pincus. His exams/ quizzes are very fair and based on the HW he gives and practice. Since Calc 2 is a hard class in general, you need to put in hours of studying, but trust me, if you do that, you're chilling in his class. I bombed the final, but with Pincus' generosity, I was able to end with an A (if he put the final in, I would've had a B+). He genuinely cares about his students and will answer any questions you have. Other than the fact that his lectures lack explanation sometimes, and you have to self-learn concepts, he is a great professor, and I highly recommend him.

Dr. Ebrahimian is a very professional guy and a talented lecturer. He will aptly answer any question to make sure everything is understood. Math 141 is a difficult course, however, and it's important to stay on top of topics by doing as much practice as you can (assigned homework problems and worksheets).
Good lecturer but is an awful grader, no curving exams or final grades. Low 70s averages with class average being in the 70s, with many kids stressing for the final to even pass the class (with a C).

Amazing professor. My class was the first he taught as a professor rather than as a TA, and he is genuinely one of the best math professors out there. His lectures are extremely well-organized, and he consistently encourages students to ask questions. Although I never personally attended his office hours, many classmates shared that he patiently works through problems with you step by step and makes sure you truly understand the material.

We had weekly quizzes, usually consisting of one or two questions taken directly from the worksheets he posted on ELMS before each quiz, which made them very fair. He also provided practice exams that closely mirrored the actual midterms. Overall, he is a great professor, and it’s clear he wants every single student to succeed.

I was scared going into Calc 2 as everyone said it was a weed out class but Professor Song was great. Exams were similar to problems solved done in class and she would tell us what would be on the weekly quizzes. Id say a better option for Calc 2

Dr Fernandes was a good teacher overall. His biggest flaw was that he relied heavily on the TAs to teach methods discussed in class. He was often slightly late and quick to leave, but he would always discuss mistakes after class as long as you walked with him. Expect a good amount of quizzes and homework. The exams are not too bad as long as you understand the problems he goes over in class. The final is daunting, but definitely possible to get an A on if you go over enough past finals and understand the processes behind the questions given. He will also curve the average to a C or -C, so if you're keeping with the average, you will pass the class. Lots of grades and a curve were posted in the last few days of class, so constantly be on top of your work and don't get discouraged.

Dr Williams is a good lecture, super intelligent, and is happy to answer any questions that you have in person. However, any other communication is spotty and could easily take multiple weeks to respond to you. During the Fall 2025 semester, he changed his office hours multiple times and only let us know the morning of. His MATH141 class is super demanding and because there are so few homework assignments to help fluff up your grade that every single assignment you have needs to be an A, or else your grade is going to plummet. Multiple people in my class compared his exams with other professor's exams and Williams' were noticeably more difficult. 
This course marks the worst grade I'll have ever gained during my entire 90 credits of higher education so far. I was literally teaching people within the course and still got a D. I know people that totally no-life'd the Fall 2025 semester as a whole and they have fine grades in the class. Not passing this class set me back an entire year in the degree pathway I was pursuing and I've resulted to completely changing my major.
I'm surprised that basically every single professor that is offered during the Spring 2026 semester is rated higher than Williams (who was the highest rated available professor when I registered for the Fall 2025 semester).
He gets a bad rep but overall a very good guy. Just go to office hours atleast once a week and do your suggested problems. everything else falls into place.

genuinely the goat bro. There's a LOT in this course so he has to go quick but he still takes the time to answer every question in depth and teach the content well. He drops the lowest hw score, 2 lowest quiz scores, and your lowest exam (if you get higher on the final). He is the best possible option for this class. The practice exams are extremely similar to the actual exam and he offers like 5 for each midterm.

Great guy but wasn't for me. I devoted about 20 hours of studying a week for this course, along with getting a tutor in the middle of the semester and still had to drop out because there was no way for me to pass. I met up with him several times in the first few weeks to create a plan to pass but it obviously wasn't working and he basically told me I wasn't going to be successful in his class. Other friends who took him loved him, but just know that you need a VERY good understanding of calculus I before you take this course.

Absolute goat. I did pretty poorly on the first 2 midterms and then reached out to him for help, and he did everything he could to help me from that point onward. His office hours are incredibly chill and helpful, and I encourage anyone struggling in his course to attend them as much as possible. He truly wants everybody to do well in his course and that is clearly reflected in his lessons, often asking for feedback and tweaking his lessons to fit people's preferences. Also one of the funniest teachers I have ever had, and he seems to really enjoy teaching. Please take him if doing well is your goal.
Don't take him, ridiculous make-up policy, never checks emails, incredibly hard tests. Only upside is his lectures are interesting. Good luck communicating with him outside of lectures.

Super good lecturer who genuinely cares. Quizzes are much easier than the exams, although the homework does take a while. Exams are pretty hard, but he gives a list of suggested problems on Canvas. If you put in the work and do all of them, it prepares you very well for the exam because he'll make a lot of the problems very similar to the suggested problems. 

Also, I once dropped my keycard in class and he drove all the way to North Campus to return it to me :) very kind

Dr. Ebrahimian was always willing to help his students, taking time to answer questions to ensure everyone understands. He is very organized in how he structured the class, to make no confusion with assignment submissions or exams. Her lectures were organized and she clearly knows the material well. She explains concepts in a straightforward way and works through examples, but sometimes the pace can feel a little fast if you’re not already comfortable with calculus. You definitely need to practice a lot on your own to do well.

The curve is just dropping the lowest quiz and worksheet scores depending on how you do on those.

He is very kind, flexible, and willing to accommodate students; he genuinely cares about you as a person and wants you to succeed. He is also basically omnipresent on emails, and you pretty much never have to wait more than a day. I got multiple responses from him within 10 minutes to an hour.

If you have to reschedule a quiz, he basically leaves it up to your TA. His TAs are chill, so this is completely fine.

He is very willing to let you reschedule exams in a timely manner, even if you don't provide documentation. I was having a breakdown with 4 exams in a single week, and he didn't miss a beat, replying in like 10 minutes, accepting my requests without any pushback.

I've never gotten anything less than 100 in his class, but from what I've heard, he is very generous with partial credit if you make a small algebra mistake but demonstrate that you understand the concept he taught you.

I already learned Calculus 1 through 3 in high school, but I just didn't take the AP exams, so lectures are kind of irrelevant to me. However, from what I've heard from people who didn't, his lectures are extremely helpful. Not derivation-heavy, pretty much just examples of problems you'll have to solve. If we don't get to something, he'll adjust the quizzes accordingly, so as to ensure you don't have to study on your own.

description: Prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in MATH140. Or 1 course with a minimum grade of B- from (MATH130, MATH136); and permission of CMNS-Mathematics department.
